source: Toprank Review Academy (TRA) Nursing Module – Complete Handout

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: After tonsillectomy, which sign most strongly suggests bleeding?
questions.rationale: Frequent swallowing indicates blood trickling down the throat.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Tonsillectomy Care (PDF p. 326)
questions.quote: Assess for post op bleeding such as frequent swallowing

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which food is restricted soon after tonsillectomy?
questions.rationale: Milk products may be restricted because they coat the throat and increase clearing.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Tonsillectomy Care (PDF p. 326)
questions.quote: Milk and milk products (ice cream and yogurt) may be restricted

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which immediate post-tonsillectomy position allows drainage from the mouth?
questions.rationale: Prone with head turned to the side lets secretions drain.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Tonsillectomy Care (PDF p. 326)
questions.quote: the most comfortable position is prone

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Severe sore throat, trismus, and drooling after tonsillitis suggest:
questions.rationale: Quinsy causes trismus, drooling, odynophagia, and possible airway obstruction.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Peritonsillar Abscess (PDF p. 326)
questions.quote: Severe sore throat, fever trismus (inability to open the mouth), and drooling.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: What is the initial sign of laryngitis?
questions.rationale: Hoarseness is initial; aphonia and cough may follow. Rest the voice.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Laryngitis (PDF p. 327)
questions.quote: Hoarseness of voice – initial sign

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which symptom warrants evaluation for laryngeal cancer?
questions.rationale: Persistent hoarseness over 2 weeks, especially in smokers and drinkers.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Cancer of the Larynx (PDF p. 327)
questions.quote: Hoarseness of voice for more than 2 weeks

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Before a total laryngectomy, the nurse should first:
questions.rationale: Total laryngectomy causes permanent voice loss; set up communication before surgery.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Laryngectomy Care (PDF p. 327)
questions.quote: Establish a method for communication before surgery

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Chronic bronchitis is diagnosed by a productive cough lasting:
questions.rationale: Productive cough at least 3 months per year for 2 consecutive years.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, COPD (PDF p. 328)
questions.quote: Presence of a productive cough lasting at least 3 months a year for 2 successive years

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: A thin client with barrel chest, pursed-lip breathing, and minimal cough is described as a:
questions.rationale: Emphysema: pink puffer, barrel chest, weight loss; bronchitis: blue bloater, productive cough.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Emphysema (PDF p. 328)
questions.quote: Pink puffer

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which test identifies a genetic cause of emphysema?
questions.rationale: Alpha-1 antitrypsin deficiency is a genetic cause.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, COPD Diagnostics (PDF p. 328)
questions.quote: Alpha-1-antitrypsin assay useful in identifying genetically determined deficiency in emphysema

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Why is pursed-lip breathing taught to a client with COPD?
questions.rationale: Pursed-lip breathing slows expiration and keeps airways open.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, COPD Interventions (PDF p. 329)
questions.quote: Pursed-lip breathing helps slow expiration, prevents collapse of small airways

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Oxygen for a client with COPD is usually given at:
questions.rationale: Low-flow oxygen avoids suppressing hypoxic drive and worsening CO2 retention.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, COPD Interventions (PDF p. 329)
questions.quote: Administer low flow of oxygen (1-2L/min)

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which meal plan suits a client with COPD who has weight loss?
questions.rationale: Small frequent meals and supplements improve intake without increasing dyspnea.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, COPD Interventions (PDF p. 329)
questions.quote: Provide small frequent meals

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which asthma medication is used for quick relief of acute symptoms?
questions.rationale: Short-acting beta2 agonists are quick-relief; the others are long-term control.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Asthma Pharmacology (PDF p. 329)
questions.quote: Short-acting beta2-adrenergic agonists

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: What are the three most common symptoms of asthma?
questions.rationale: Cough, dyspnea, and wheezing are most common.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Bronchial Asthma (PDF p. 329)
questions.quote: Three most common symptoms of asthma

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Chronic cough with copious purulent sputum, hemoptysis, and clubbing suggests:
questions.rationale: Bronchiectasis is irreversible bronchial dilation with copious purulent sputum.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Bronchiectasis (PDF p. 330)
questions.quote: Chronic cough with copious amount of purulent sputum

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which technique should the family of a client with bronchiectasis learn?
questions.rationale: Postural drainage and chest physiotherapy help clear secretions.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Bronchiectasis (PDF p. 330)
questions.quote: Educate the patient and his family in performing postural drainage

questions.subject: NP I
questions.stem: A gold miner with silicosis has a positive tuberculin test. The nurse anticipates:
questions.rationale: Silicosis increases TB risk; give prophylactic INH if tuberculin-positive.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Occupational Lung Diseases (PDF p. 330)
questions.quote: Give prophylactic isoniazid (INH) to patient with positive tuberculin test

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Tracheal deviation away from the injured side with hypotension indicates:
questions.rationale: Trapped air causes mediastinal shift away from the affected side.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Tension Pneumothorax (PDF p. 331)
questions.quote: Tracheal deviation away from affected side in tension pneumothorax

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: What is the immediate management of tension pneumothorax?
questions.rationale: Immediate decompression prevents cardiovascular collapse, followed by chest tube.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Tension Pneumothorax (PDF p. 331)
questions.quote: Immediate decompression to prevent cardiovascular collapse

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: A client has a sucking stab wound to the chest. The nurse's first action is to:
questions.rationale: Close the open wound immediately with an occlusive (petroleum) dressing.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Open Pneumothorax (PDF p. 331)
questions.quote: Apply petroleum gauze to sucking chest wound

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: After thoracentesis for pleural effusion, the nurse should:
options: Record amount and send to lab
Lay client flat on puncture side immediately
questions.rationale: Record the amount of fluid aspirated and send it for laboratory analysis.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Pleural Effusion (PDF p. 332)
questions.quote: Record the amount of fluid aspirated and send it to the laboratory

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Sharp, knifelike chest pain worse on deep inspiration with a friction rub suggests:
questions.rationale: Inflamed pleural layers rub during respiration, causing localized pleuritic pain.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Pleurisy (PDF p. 332)
questions.quote: severe, sharp, knifelike pain

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Blood in the pleural space after chest trauma is called:
questions.rationale: Hemothorax may cause hidden blood loss; treated with chest tube and volume replacement.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Hemothorax (PDF p. 332)
questions.quote: Blood in pleural space as a result of penetrating or blunt chest trauma
